For any admissible funding amount, after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract's entire balance has been transferred out so address(c).balance == 0; the mutant omits the transfer, leaving the balance unchanged (positive) for some funded amount.

For any caller, a withdrawAll call may only succeed (and only then may contract funds move) if the caller is the contract owner; the mutant lets any non-owner successfully drain the contract, so the rule fails for some non-owner caller.

For any caller other than the owner and any funded balance, calling withdrawAll must not decrease the contract's balance (onlyOwner enforces this); the mutant lets a non-owner drain it, so the balance drops for some caller/amount.

For any non-owner caller and any positive amount held by the contract, calling withdrawAll must fail and leave the contract balance unchanged (onlyOwner access control); the mutant lets the non-owner drain it, so the balance drops for some input.

For any actor and any funding, a successful withdrawAll may only be performed by the contract owner: the rule asserts that whenever the call succeeds, msg.sender equals c.owner(); the mutant lets any non-owner's withdrawAll succeed, so it fails for some non-owner input while the reference always reverts for non-owners.

For any owner and any value, after depositing funds and calling withdraw(value), c's ETH balance decreases by exactly value (the contract actually pays out); the mutant sends nothing so its balance never decreases.

For any admissible value, after funding the contract with that value and having the owner call withdraw(value), the contract's ETH balance becomes 0 (withdraw actually pays out msg.sender); the mutant's withdraw sends nothing, so the balance stays at value.

For any owner call withdraw(v) with v < the contract's balance, the contract's balance afterwards is exactly balance_before - v; the mutant instead drains the entire balance, breaking the rule whenever v < balance.

For any owner-initiated withdraw(v) where v <= the contract's balance, the contract keeps exactly balance_before - v (and only transfers v); the mutant drains the entire balance, violating this whenever v < balance.

For any owner call withdraw(v) with 0 <= v < the contract's balance, the reference C leaves exactly balance_before - v in the contract (transfers only v), whereas the mutant drains the entire balance, breaking the rule whenever v < balance.

For any amount, withdrawing as owner credits the caller with exactly that amount (caller's balance increases by the withdrawn value); the mutant sends the funds to the zero address instead, so the caller's balance does not increase.

For any admissible amount, a successful withdraw by the owner transfers exactly that amount to the caller (caller's balance increases by the value and c's balance decreases accordingly); the mutant pays the zero address instead, so the caller's balance never increases for some amount.
